docs.text: Pato Nego A buyer registers through Gateway, signs in, and orders products priced in US dollars. The order belongs to that buyer. When the buyer asks for a total in Brazilian reais, Order calls Exchange for the Banco Central do Brasil PTAX sell rate. The stored price stays in dollars. Demonstrated purchase On November 20, 2026, the public EC2 and EKS gateways each accepted an order for two units at USD 4.25. The order list and detail both showed USD 8.50. At the quoted rate of 5.8889, Order returned BRL 50.06. A second signed-in account received 404 for the same order and had an empty order list. The test accounts and product were removed after the check. Watch all six APIs running in EKS and the purchase through the public gateway . The load-test recording shows Gateway autoscaling under load. The Product and Order owners maintain their source repositories. The parent repository configures the shared EKS deployment. Course delivery instructions AI assistance AI assisted with Python Exchange, Gateway integration, Kubernetes manifests, infrastructure configuration, CI configuration, end-to-end verification and this documentation. The test figures come from recorded runs. Individual members should credit their own contributions in their personal submissions.

docs.text: São Paulo operating costs The estimate uses 730 hours per month, USD on-demand rates and the November 20, 2026 inventory in sa-east-1. The four public IPv4 addresses cover the existing gateway, the two teammates’ public hosts and the NAT gateway. The RDS instance has seven-day backup retention. These are list-price projections before credits, taxes, usage-based charges and discounts. EC2 deployment Quantity and rate USD/month Product, Order and Exchange compute 3 × t3.micro at 0.0168/hour 36.79 Identity compute 1 × t3.small at 0.0336/hour 24.53 Gateway compute 1 × t3.medium at 0.0672/hour 49.06 EC2 disks 86 GB gp3 at 0.152/GB-month 13.07 PostgreSQL compute Single-AZ db.t4g.micro at 0.034/hour 24.82 PostgreSQL disk 20 GB gp3 at 0.219/GB-month 4.38 Outbound network 1 NAT at 0.093/hour 67.89 Public IPv4 4 at 0.005/hour 14.60 Existing fixed-cost estimate 235.14 Additional EKS deployment USD/month Standard-support control plane at 0.10/hour 73.00 Two t3.medium workers 98.11 Two 20 GB worker disks at 0.152/GB-month if gp3 6.08 One load balancer at 0.034/hour 24.82 Incremental estimate before usage 202.01 An internet-facing load balancer with two public IPv4 addresses adds about USD 7.30/month. An internal load balancer uses private addresses. NAT adds USD 0.093 per GB processed. Load-balancer capacity or processed bytes, registry storage, cross-AZ traffic, internet egress, burst credits and excess backup storage depend on usage. The existing VPC, NAT and RDS are shared across the two environments. Reproduce the estimate with the São Paulo region and the quantities above. AWS Pricing Calculator · AWS Price List · EKS pricing The account’s AWS Pricing Calculator workload estimate Pato-Nego-Sao-Paulo-EC2-and-EKS returned USD 444.45/month for 13 line items. This includes the two public load-balancer addresses. Find the saved workload estimate in Billing and Cost Management → Pricing Calculator. Cost Explorer reported preliminary São Paulo regional unblended costs of USD 0.90 on November 18 and USD 7.06 on November 19, before EKS provisioning. Those are account-wide daily observations. CodeBuild deployment minutes and ECR image storage add usage charges. Managed services and availability RDS manages PostgreSQL backups and patching. EKS operates the Kubernetes control plane. The group remains responsible for application rollouts, database migrations, worker capacity and recovery. The EC2 app has single service hosts and a single-AZ database. A database outage can stop purchases even when Gateway and Exchange are healthy. A proposed course-demo objective is 99% successful authenticated reads per month and p95 below 500 ms for cached catalog reads at ten concurrent users. Count unexpected 5xx responses and timeouts as failures. Exclude deliberately invalid test requests. At 99% availability a 30-day month allows 7 hours 12 minutes of downtime. The short local measurements support the latency target under that workload. A monthly availability claim needs continuous end-to-end measurements. Load-test results

docs.text: Kubernetes deployment The Pato Nego EKS cluster uses sa-east-1. The CloudFormation stack creates a managed control plane, a shared worker in one Availability Zone and a dedicated Exchange worker in another. Both workers use private subnets and the existing NAT gateway. The Kubernetes API accepts connections from the VPC and the administrator’s configured IP. The EC2 application has a separate gateway and continues serving its original users. Workload Kubernetes service Deployment inputs Gateway gateway, HTTPS 443 Gateway TLS Secret and routing ConfigMap Auth auth, HTTP 8080 JWT signing Secret and token lifetime Account account, HTTP 8080 Dedicated database credentials and regional RDS CA Exchange exchange, HTTP 8000 PTAX timeout and cache durations Product product, HTTP 8080 Product database credentials, RDS CA and Redis address Order order, HTTP 8080 Order database credentials, RDS CA and Product/Exchange addresses Redis product-redis, TCP 6379 In-memory Product detail cache Each service keeps its Kubernetes resources in its own repository’s k8s/ directory. Order defines its Deployment, Service and autoscaler together in api/order-service/k8s/k8s.yaml . Account, Auth and Gateway consume Secrets whose values are provisioned directly in the namespace. Exchange consumes public Bacen data and uses the authenticated account ID forwarded by Gateway. Internal calls resolve services by their Kubernetes DNS names. Exchange runs on the node labeled workload=exchange . Verify the cluster With an authorized AWS identity and network path to the API, use the following commands. aws eks update-kubeconfig --region sa-east-1 --name pato-nego kubectl get nodes -L workload,topology.kubernetes.io/zone kubectl -n pato-nego get deployments,services,hpa kubectl -n pato-nego get endpointslices kubectl -n pato-nego rollout status deployment/exchange kubectl -n pato-nego top pods The cluster deployment uses the built service images in private ECR by digest. The checked-in image tags ending in :local are for locally built images. For deployment, override the image name and digest with Kustomize. Generate the JWT key outside Git. For Account, populate its Secret with the RDS hostname, database, username and password and put the regional RDS certificate bundle in the rds-ca ConfigMap under bundle.pem . For Gateway, create the gateway-tls TLS Secret before applying the manifest. HTTPS demo Gateway terminates TLS behind an internet-facing Network Load Balancer. The EKS demonstration uses its own self-signed public certificate , valid through May 20, 2027. Download the certificate and use it to verify the HTTPS connection. Browsers require an explicit trust decision for this certificate. For ongoing public use, the group can install a publicly trusted certificate for a domain it controls. Reissue the certificate if the load-balancer hostname changes. curl --cacert gateway.pem https://a696ab569ad9e4c62ae41bd9b2743a49-970d0868192873ca.elb.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com/health-check The EKS namespace has an independent JWT key and an isolated database on the existing RDS instance. The public load-balancer smoke test passed with certificate verification, and the original EC2 gateway also returned 200 after the EKS release. Account verifies the RDS hostname and regional CA. Connectivity tests covered registration, login, account lookup, a live USD/BRL quote, the quote cache, logout and anonymous access control. Product and Order on the shared worker Gateway routes to product:8080 and order:8080 . Order fetches product prices from Product and the USD/BRL quote from exchange:8000 . Product caches repeated catalog detail reads in product-redis:6379 . Only Gateway has a public load balancer. The parent repository pins both service revisions and their ECR image digests. Its Kustomize overlay reads the pinned manifests directly from the two submodules. It assigns Product, Order and Redis to the existing shared worker. Exchange stays on its dedicated worker. Reapply from the parent checkout with its submodules initialized: kubectl kustomize --load-restrictor LoadRestrictionsNone infra/k8s/store | kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pato-store -f - kubectl -n pato-nego rollout status deployment/product-redis kubectl -n pato-nego rollout status deployment/product kubectl -n pato-nego rollout status deployment/order The render command reads files outside the overlay directory from the pinned local submodules. On a fresh namespace, provision the rds-ca ConfigMap with key bundle.pem and populate the following Secrets before deploying. Each application's login owns its own EKS database on the existing PostgreSQL instance. The overlay maps the CA bundle to the filename required by each service. Secret Required keys Database product-credentials DATABASE_HOST , DATABASE_NAME , DATABASE_USERNAME , DATABASE_PASSWORD pato_eks_product order-secrets DATABASE_HOST , DATABASE_USERNAME , DATABASE_PASSWORD pato_eks_order , selected in order-config A rollout initially exhausted PostgreSQL connections when overlapping replicas opened their default pools. Each EKS Product and Order replica now keeps one idle connection and can use up to three. Both apps request 125m CPU. Their autoscalers target 100% of that request, preserving the original 125m CPU threshold. A supervised scale check brought Product and Order to two Ready replicas each at the same time on the shared worker. The autoscalers were then restored to their normal range of one to three. Simultaneous scale-out across several services is limited by the capacity of the shared worker. Watch the cluster and purchase demonstration . Delivery pipeline Exchange GitHub Actions builds the container, runs the Python tests inside it, starts the server and checks the health and authentication responses. The workflow supports Docker Hub publication and an EKS rollout by digest when the registry and EKS settings are configured. The configured release publishes to private ECR, and CodeBuild runs inside the VPC. On November 20 the GitHub release and CodeBuild both succeeded. The running pod image matched the ECR digest sha256:1a9d314ec0e5ad83e187893f4e877feb8cbe8cd9e9223d8d739c090ac8c89878 . Docker Hub publication requires separate registry credentials. Exchange workflow

docs.text: Load tests and bottlenecks Local buying and catalog workloads Tested November 20, 2026 with k6 1.5.0 and Docker Compose. Each measured run lasted 15 seconds with 10 virtual users and a 100 ms pause between operations. Setup created a disposable authenticated account and a test product. The detail comparison used two runs per cache setting after a 6-second warm-up. All timed traffic went through Gateway on the local Docker network. The order workload used USD. The measurements exclude setup requests and do not exercise the PTAX API. Product was at 668bac8 and Order-service at ae05a60 . Gateway and Exchange used the local integration changes. Scenario Requests Requests/s p95 Errors Product detail, cache disabled (1) 1266 79.1 31.04 ms 0.00% Product detail, cache disabled (2) 1330 84.6 18.32 ms 0.00% Product detail, Redis (1) 1360 87.0 13.96 ms 0.00% Product detail, Redis (2) 1364 87.3 13.87 ms 0.00% Catalog list 1292 82.6 18.55 ms 0.00% Create order (USD) 1036 66.3 58.09 ms 0.00% Download the six measured k6 summaries . Cache comparison Disabled mean of the two run p95 values was 24.68 ms. Redis reported 0 hits during the measured runs. Redis mean of the two run p95 values was 13.91 ms. Redis reported 2,724 hits during the measured runs. These measurements apply to this short, single-host workload. The EKS run below exercises a different endpoint. Exchange under concurrent load Each Exchange process caches Bacen bulletins by currency for 300 seconds. A lock per currency lets one caller refresh while others reuse its result. Different currency codes can refresh independently. After a provider timeout, Exchange serves the last quote if available and retries after 30 seconds. With a cold cache, a provider failure returns 502. Rates and timestamps come from Bacen. Each new replica starts with a cold cache. The Exchange tests simulate the clock and a Bacen timeout. The production check requested USD/BRL through both Gateway routes and observed a cache hit. These checks cover provider calls and fallback behavior. The table above measures a separate cache in Product. Exchange source and tests Gateway autoscaling on EKS On November 20, 2026, k6 ran inside the São Paulo cluster. It targeted HTTPS GET /health-check on the Spring Boot Gateway at 180 scheduled requests per second for two minutes, with up to 24 virtual users. The HPA targeted 50% utilization of a 250m CPU request, with a minimum of one and a maximum of three replicas. Kubernetes reported a CPU-triggered resize from one to three, and all three Gateway pods became ready. Completed HTTP requests HTTP failures Delivered rate p95 Dropped scheduled iterations 21,553 0 179.60/s 39.03 ms 48 The generator dropped 48 iterations before sending an HTTP request. The success rate applies to requests it sent. This in-cluster workload measures Gateway health handling and scale-out. The EC2 purchase and EKS authentication checks exercise other services separately. Watch the 80-second recording of k6, the HPA and the pods · Read the k6 summary .
